html:
The Cayubaba are an Indigenous people of the Bolivian Amazon, in the Beni region west of the Mamoré river. Their language is an isolate, related to no other known language, and today only a handful of elders speak it; around 800 people identify as Cayubaba.

The Beni plains, called Moxos, flood every year, and its earlier peoples built raised fields, causeways and mounds. In the late 1600s and 1700s Jesuit missions gathered many peoples of Moxos into towns, much like the reductions further south; the Cayubaba were settled at the mission of Exaltación. Later, the rubber boom took many as workers. Their lands lie in Bolivia.
